editorial:
Imagine you are married to a private eye who keeps secrets, but you are just as curious as he is. That is the fun setup here. You get to follow Bill Reardon, a detective trying to solve a jewelry heist, while his wife decides she wants in on the action. Instead of staying home, she pops up everywhere, trying to help him catch the bad guys. It feels like a classic game of cat and mouse, but the cat is a bored wife and the mouse is a husband who just wants to do his job in peace. The whole vibe is light, breezy, and full of old-school charm.

The acting is great because the chemistry between the lead couple keeps the energy high. You will love how the mystery unfolds, even if some parts feel a bit slow by today's standards. The best part is seeing the frustration on Bill's face every time his wife ruins a lead. If you enjoy a good laugh mixed with a crime caper, you should definitely give this a try. Since it is an older gem, you might want to look for a high-quality digital rental on Apple TV or see if you can find a restored 4K Blu-ray to add to your physical collection for the best picture quality.
endingExplained: Everything comes to a head when the jewelry thief is finally cornered. Bill manages to solve the case, but not without his wife getting in the way one last time. The twist is that her meddling actually helps uncover a key clue that Bill missed. After the criminals are arrested, the couple makes peace. The movie ends with a funny nod to their relationship, showing that Bill might be the detective, but his wife is the real boss.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves old-fashioned detective stories and funny marriages.
